info.name: ClinicalHarmony · Phase 5 — US Core structural validation + FHIR generation
info.description: Phase 5 endpoints (/api/fhir-compliance/*): structural US Core required-field validation, rule catalog + live toggle, and FHIR generation persisted to Gold. Validate and rule GETs are public; generate and rule toggle need clinicalharmony/pipeline.write. Make sure `docker-compose up -d` is running. Run '0b. Auth' first: it does a client_credentials grant against Keycloak (realm clinicalharmony, {{keycloak_url}}) and stores the token in the collection variable access_token, which every request inherits via the collection's Bearer auth (public endpoints ignore it). Tokens live 5 minutes — re-run 0b when you get 401s.

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, body `{"status":"UP"}`. If this fails, the container isn't running — check `docker ps` for clinicalharmony-fhir-compliance-service.

SMART Backend Services-style client_credentials grant (client secret via HTTP Basic). Requests every SMART read scope plus the clinicalharmony/pipeline.write operational scope; the test script stores the token in {{access_token}}, which the collection's Bearer auth sends on every request. Expect: 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 300, and scope echoing what was granted.

Expect: 200 OK, a JSON array of 7 rules — one per US Core resource type (USCORE_PATIENT_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_CONDITION_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_OBSERVATION_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_MEDICATIONREQUEST_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_ALLERGYINTOLERANCE_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_ENCOUNTER_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_DIAGNOSTICREPORT_COMPLETENESS). Each has ruleCode, ruleName, category, severity, active, and expression (the requiredFields list).

Expect: 200 OK. Look at `expression.requiredFields` — ["id","identifier","name","gender","birthDate"]. This is exactly what request #5 below checks a Patient resource against. Try GET .../rules/NOT_A_REAL_CODE afterward — expect 404.

Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: false`. resourceResults has 4 entries — p1 valid:true (has everything), p2 valid:false (missing identifier/name/birthDate — read the `reason` field), m1 valid:true (has medicationReference, satisfying the medication[x] choice), m2 valid:false (missing BOTH medicationCodeableConcept and medicationReference — see how missingFields shows them joined with '|', meaning 'either one would have worked'). validationReportIds has 2 entries (one per failure) — go check `silver.validation_reports` in DBeaver/psql for those ids and you'll see the same reason text persisted there.

item.name: 4. Validate — unsupported resource type is skipped, not failed

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: true`, `resourceResults: []`. Practitioner has no USCORE_* rule registered, so it's silently skipped rather than counted as a failure — same 'skip what you don't own' convention as rules-engine-service's RuleExecutor. This is the behavior request #8 below exercises deliberately via a toggle.

item.name: 5. Generate — full patient record, all 7 resource types

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, a FHIR Bundle (`resourceType: "Bundle"`, `type: "collection"`) with 7 entries — one Patient (id patient-901) plus one each of Condition/Observation/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance/Encounter/DiagnosticReport. Note the real terminology system URIs in each `code.coding[0].system` (e.g. http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm for the Condition). After this call, check `gold.fhir_resources` in psql/DBeaver — you should see all 7 rows with `is_us_core_compliant = true`.

Expect: 200 OK, a Bundle with exactly 1 entry (just the Patient — no name given, so the `name` field is omitted entirely rather than sent as null; look for that). Confirms every item list is genuinely optional.
Expect: 200 OK, the rule object with `active: false`. This takes effect immediately — no restart needed.

item.name: 8. Validate again — toggled-off rule is now skipped

request.description: Run this right after #7. Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: true`, `resourceResults: []` — the SAME incomplete Patient that failed in request #3 is now skipped, because its rule is inactive. This proves the toggle works live. Run request #9 next to restore it before you forget.
Expect: 200 OK, `active: true`. Always run this after #7/#8 so the rule catalog is back to its normal state for anyone testing after you.
